title: Local criterion for a locally finite type scheme to be unramified over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The morphism is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if every point $y\in Y$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points], the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ equals its residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $\kappa(y)/k$ is a finite separable algebraic extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Empty $Y$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), parts (1) and (2), local-ring and residue-field characterization

proof.text: Suppose $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified. By [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition], $Y$ has an open partition by $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ with $L_i/k$ finite separable. Apply [lem-trf-disjoint-field-spectra-point-stalk-data] to this partition: every point is closed, the canonical local-ring residue quotient is an isomorphism, and $\kappa(y_i)\simeq L_i$ over $k$. Thus its residue extension is finite separable, as required; the empty partition is included.

Conversely assume the pointwise conditions and fix $y\in Y$. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point $s=f(y)$ with $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k,s}=k$, whose maximal ideal is $0$, and $\kappa(s)=k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-residue-field]. The hypothesis that the canonical quotient $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism means $\mathfrak m_y=0=\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, and $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s)=\kappa(y)/k$ is finite separable algebraic. Since $f$ is locally of finite type, [lem-trf-stalk-formally-unramified-maximal-residue-criterion] (direction from the two conditions) shows that the actual stalk map $f_y^\sharp:k\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is formally unramified.

source.place: Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), (6) implies (1) at the stalk, for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$

proof.text: As $y$ varies, step 2 gives formal unramifiedness of every actual stalk map of $f$. Apply [lem-trf-formally-unramified-from-all-stalks] to deduce that $f$ is formally unramified. No finite covering assumption is involved.

source.place: Tag 04E8 (lemma-formally-unramified-local), (3) implies (1), globalized to schemes by More on Morphisms Tag 0HAL (lemma-formally-unramified), (4) implies (1). Mathlib packages this globalization in HasRingHomProperty.of_stalkMap.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis and formally unramified by step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified]: its diagonal is an open immersion, so $f$ is unramified. Together with step 1 this proves the equivalence. The converse only uses the assumed canonical residue isomorphisms and finite separability, and also applies to empty $Y$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), part (1), with Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point) (6) implies (1) for the stalk criterion and More on Morphisms 02HE; Algebra 04E8 and More on Morphisms 0HAL give global formal unramifiedness from stalks.
